title: Proposal
description: How an agent raises a problem it found on its own, rather than waiting to be told. Requiring evidence and a proposed work order is what separates a proposal from a suggestion: the boss triages against something checkable. Open proposals are capped per agent, because an idle agent with no cap generates work to justify its own existence, and that costs real money.

triagedBy.description: The boss who ruled on it. Present once triage has happened.

problem.description: What is wrong, stated as an observation rather than an opinion.

evidence.description: Evidence records, file paths or seeds that substantiate the problem. A proposal with no evidence is an opinion, and the schema refuses it.

proposedWork.description: The concrete change proposed. Vague proposals push the thinking onto the boss, which is the opposite of what a proactive agent is for.

estimatedCost.description: What acting on this is expected to cost, in the studio's currency. Absent means the proposer could not estimate it, which is itself worth knowing.

decision.description: The boss's reasoning. Required on rejection: an agent told 'no' with no reason will simply propose it again next week.

taskId.description: The work order this became, once accepted.

allOf.description: An accepted proposal becomes a work order, or it was not really accepted.
A rejection must carry its reasoning, so the same proposal does not return unchanged.
